candidates.label: Pergamon archaeological site
candidates.support: The extensively excavated acropolis and lower city near modern Bergama, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, are undisputed as ancient Pergamon; the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's coordinate for the site (on the acropolis) and Wikidata's coordinate agree closely.

summary.text: Pergamon was founded in the 3rd century BC as the capital of the Attalid dynasty and, per UNESCO, became a major cultural, scientific and political hub of the Hellenistic world, with one of antiquity's largest libraries; after passing to Rome in 133 BC it served as capital of the Roman province of Asia. It is addressed in Revelation 2 as one of the seven churches, described there as the place 'where Satan's throne is.'

history.text: After the last Attalid king bequeathed his kingdom to Rome in 133 BC, Pergamon became a metropolis of the Roman province of Asia; in the Byzantine period, though reduced to a middle-sized town, it remained a religious centre as the home of one of the seven churches of Revelation.
